scene.label: Act 1, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. Tarsus. A room in the Governor's house.
scene.location: Tarsus. A room in the Governor's house.

content.text: Enter Cleon, the governor of Tarsus, with Dionyza and others.

lines.text: My Dionyza, shall we rest us here,
lines.plainText: My Dionyza shall we rest us here

lines.text: And by relating tales of others' griefs,
lines.plainText: And by relating tales of others' griefs

lines.text: See if 'twill teach us to forget our own?
lines.plainText: See if 'twill teach us to forget our own

lines.text: That were to blow at fire in hope to quench it;
lines.plainText: That were to blow at fire in hope to quench it

lines.text: For who digs hills because they do aspire
lines.plainText: For who digs hills because they do aspire

lines.text: Throws down one mountain to cast up a higher.
lines.plainText: Throws down one mountain to cast up a higher

lines.text: O my distressed lord, even such our griefs are;
lines.plainText: O my distressed lord even such our griefs are

lines.text: Here they're but felt, and seen with mischief's eyes,
lines.plainText: Here they're but felt and seen with mischief's eyes

lines.text: But like to groves, being topp'd, they higher rise.
lines.plainText: But like to groves being topp'd they higher rise

lines.text: O Dionyza,
lines.plainText: O Dionyza

lines.text: Who wanteth food, and will not say he wants it,
lines.plainText: Who wanteth food and will not say he wants it

lines.text: Or can conceal his hunger till he famish?
lines.plainText: Or can conceal his hunger till he famish

lines.text: Our tongues and sorrows do sound deep
lines.plainText: Our tongues and sorrows do sound deep

lines.text: Our woes into the air; our eyes do weep,
lines.plainText: Our woes into the air our eyes do weep

lines.text: Till tongues fetch breath that may proclaim them louder;
lines.plainText: Till tongues fetch breath that may proclaim them louder

lines.text: That, if heaven slumber while their creatures want,
lines.plainText: That if heaven slumber while their creatures want

lines.text: They may awake their helps to comfort them.
lines.plainText: They may awake their helps to comfort them

lines.text: I'll then discourse our woes, felt several years,
lines.plainText: I'll then discourse our woes felt several years

lines.text: And wanting breath to speak, help me with tears.
lines.plainText: And wanting breath to speak help me with tears

lines.text: I'll do my best, sir.
lines.plainText: I'll do my best sir

lines.text: This Tarsus, o'er which I have the government,
lines.plainText: This Tarsus o'er which I have the government

lines.text: A city on whom plenty held full hand,
lines.plainText: A city on whom plenty held full hand

lines.text: For riches strew'd herself even in the streets;
lines.plainText: For riches strew'd herself even in the streets

lines.text: Whose towers bore heads so high they kiss'd the clouds,
lines.plainText: Whose towers bore heads so high they kiss'd the clouds

lines.text: And strangers ne'er beheld but wonder'd at;
lines.plainText: And strangers ne'er beheld but wonder'd at

lines.text: Whose men and dames so jetted and adorn'd,
lines.plainText: Whose men and dames so jetted and adorn'd

lines.text: Like one another's glass to trim them by:
lines.plainText: Like one another's glass to trim them by

lines.text: Their tables were stored full to glad the sight,
lines.plainText: Their tables were stored full to glad the sight

lines.text: And not so much to feed on as delight;
lines.plainText: And not so much to feed on as delight

lines.text: All poverty was scorn'd, and pride so great,
lines.plainText: All poverty was scorn'd and pride so great

lines.text: The name of help grew odious to repeat.
lines.plainText: The name of help grew odious to repeat

lines.text: O, 'tis too true.
lines.plainText: O 'tis too true

lines.text: But see what heaven can do! By this our change,
lines.plainText: But see what heaven can do By this our change

lines.text: These mouths, who but of late, earth, sea, and air,
lines.plainText: These mouths who but of late earth sea and air

lines.text: Were all too little to content and please,
lines.plainText: Were all too little to content and please

lines.text: Although they gave their creatures in abundance,
lines.plainText: Although they gave their creatures in abundance

lines.text: As houses are defiled for want of use,
lines.plainText: As houses are defiled for want of use

lines.text: They are now starved for want of exercise:
lines.plainText: They are now starved for want of exercise

lines.text: Those palates who, not yet two summers younger,
lines.plainText: Those palates who not yet two summers younger

lines.text: Must have inventions to delight the taste,
lines.plainText: Must have inventions to delight the taste

lines.text: Would now be glad of bread and beg for it:
lines.plainText: Would now be glad of bread and beg for it

lines.text: Those mothers who, to nousle up their babes,
lines.plainText: Those mothers who to nousle up their babes

lines.text: Thought nought too curious, are ready now
lines.plainText: Thought nought too curious are ready now

lines.text: To eat those little darlings whom they loved.
lines.plainText: To eat those little darlings whom they loved

lines.text: So sharp are hunger's teeth, that man and wife
lines.plainText: So sharp are hunger's teeth that man and wife

lines.text: Draw lots who first shall die to lengthen life:
lines.plainText: Draw lots who first shall die to lengthen life

lines.text: Here stands a lord, and there a lady weeping;
lines.plainText: Here stands a lord and there a lady weeping

lines.text: Here many sink, yet those which see them fall
lines.plainText: Here many sink yet those which see them fall

lines.text: Have scarce strength left to give them burial.
lines.plainText: Have scarce strength left to give them burial

lines.text: Is not this true?
lines.plainText: Is not this true

lines.text: Our cheeks and hollow eyes do witness it.
lines.plainText: Our cheeks and hollow eyes do witness it

lines.text: O, let those cities that of plenty's cup
lines.plainText: O let those cities that of plenty's cup

lines.text: And her prosperities so largely taste,
lines.plainText: And her prosperities so largely taste

lines.text: With their superflous riots, hear these tears!
lines.plainText: With their superflous riots hear these tears

lines.text: The misery of Tarsus may be theirs.
lines.plainText: The misery of Tarsus may be theirs

lines.text: Where's the lord governor?
lines.plainText: Where's the lord governor

lines.text: Here.
lines.plainText: Here

lines.text: Speak out thy sorrows which thou bring'st in haste,
lines.plainText: Speak out thy sorrows which thou bring'st in haste

lines.text: For comfort is too far for us to expect.
lines.plainText: For comfort is too far for us to expect

lines.text: We have descried, upon our neighbouring shore,
lines.plainText: We have descried upon our neighbouring shore

lines.text: A portly sail of ships make hitherward.
lines.plainText: A portly sail of ships make hitherward

lines.text: I thought as much.
lines.plainText: I thought as much

lines.text: One sorrow never comes but brings an heir,
lines.plainText: One sorrow never comes but brings an heir

lines.text: That may succeed as his inheritor;
lines.plainText: That may succeed as his inheritor

lines.text: And so in ours: some neighbouring nation,
lines.plainText: And so in ours some neighbouring nation

lines.text: Taking advantage of our misery,
lines.plainText: Taking advantage of our misery

lines.text: That stuff'd the hollow vessels with their power,
lines.plainText: That stuff'd the hollow vessels with their power

lines.text: To beat us down, the which are down already;
lines.plainText: To beat us down the which are down already

lines.text: And make a conquest of unhappy me,
lines.plainText: And make a conquest of unhappy me

lines.text: Whereas no glory's got to overcome.
lines.plainText: Whereas no glory's got to overcome

lines.text: That's the least fear; for, by the semblance
lines.plainText: That's the least fear for by the semblance

lines.text: Of their white flags display'd, they bring us peace,
lines.plainText: Of their white flags display'd they bring us peace

lines.text: And come to us as favourers, not as foes.
lines.plainText: And come to us as favourers not as foes

lines.text: Thou speak'st like him's untutor'd to repeat:
lines.plainText: Thou speak'st like him's untutor'd to repeat

lines.text: Who makes the fairest show means most deceit.
lines.plainText: Who makes the fairest show means most deceit

lines.text: But bring they what they will and what they can,
lines.plainText: But bring they what they will and what they can

lines.text: What need we fear?
lines.plainText: What need we fear

lines.text: The ground's the lowest, and we are half way there.
lines.plainText: The ground's the lowest and we are half way there

lines.text: Go tell their general we attend him here,
lines.plainText: Go tell their general we attend him here

lines.text: To know for what he comes, and whence he comes,
lines.plainText: To know for what he comes and whence he comes

lines.text: And what he craves.
lines.plainText: And what he craves

lines.text: I go, my lord.
lines.plainText: I go my lord

lines.text: Welcome is peace, if he on peace consist;
lines.plainText: Welcome is peace if he on peace consist

lines.text: If wars, we are unable to resist.
lines.plainText: If wars we are unable to resist

lines.text: Lord governor, for so we hear you are,
lines.plainText: Lord governor for so we hear you are

lines.text: Let not our ships and number of our men
lines.plainText: Let not our ships and number of our men

lines.text: Be like a beacon fired to amaze your eyes.
lines.plainText: Be like a beacon fired to amaze your eyes

lines.text: We have heard your miseries as far as Tyre,
lines.plainText: We have heard your miseries as far as Tyre

lines.text: And seen the desolation of your streets:
lines.plainText: And seen the desolation of your streets

lines.text: Nor come we to add sorrow to your tears,
lines.plainText: Nor come we to add sorrow to your tears

lines.text: But to relieve them of their heavy load;
lines.plainText: But to relieve them of their heavy load

lines.text: And these our ships, you happily may think
lines.plainText: And these our ships you happily may think

lines.text: Are like the Trojan horse was stuff'd within
lines.plainText: Are like the Trojan horse was stuff'd within

lines.text: With bloody veins, expecting overthrow,
lines.plainText: With bloody veins expecting overthrow

lines.text: Are stored with corn to make your needy bread,
lines.plainText: Are stored with corn to make your needy bread

lines.text: And give them life whom hunger starved half dead.
lines.plainText: And give them life whom hunger starved half dead

lines.text: The gods of Greece protect you!
lines.plainText: The gods of Greece protect you

lines.text: And we'll pray for you.
lines.plainText: And we'll pray for you

lines.text: Arise, I pray you, rise:
lines.plainText: Arise I pray you rise

lines.text: We do not look for reverence, but for love,
lines.plainText: We do not look for reverence but for love

lines.text: And harbourage for ourself, our ships and men.
lines.plainText: And harbourage for ourself our ships and men

lines.text: The which when any shall not gratify,
lines.plainText: The which when any shall not gratify

lines.text: Or pay you with unthankfulness in thought,
lines.plainText: Or pay you with unthankfulness in thought

lines.text: Be it our wives, our children, or ourselves,
lines.plainText: Be it our wives our children or ourselves

lines.text: The curse of heaven and men succeed their evils!
lines.plainText: The curse of heaven and men succeed their evils

lines.text: Till when,—the which I hope shall ne'er be seen,—
lines.plainText: Till whenthe which I hope shall ne'er be seen

lines.text: Your grace is welcome to our town and us.
lines.plainText: Your grace is welcome to our town and us

lines.text: Which welcome we'll accept; feast here awhile,
lines.plainText: Which welcome we'll accept feast here awhile

lines.text: Until our stars that frown lend us a smile.
lines.plainText: Until our stars that frown lend us a smile
